title: Best BI and dashboard tools for SQL Server (2026): 9 tools compared on Azure SQL, live queries, and security
summary: Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, and Grafana all query SQL Server live, but differ on gateways, Azure SQL sign-in, row-level security, and price. 9 tools compared.
body_markdown:
The best BI tools for SQL Server in November 2026 are Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, Grafana, and Qlik Cloud Analytics, with Omni, Zoho Analytics, Apache Superset, and Basedash covering narrower needs. Power BI is the default for Microsoft 365 organizations because it can pass each viewer’s Entra ID identity to Azure SQL, so the database enforces its own security. Metabase is the most approachable option for non-technical users and is free to self-host. Grafana is the right pick for operational dashboards and alerts. Basedash suits teams that want to ask questions in plain English against SQL Server without building a semantic model first.


Most SQL Server shortlists come down to three questions: can the tool reach an on-premises server without a gateway project, does it query live or from extracts, and can it restrict rows per viewer.


## How we evaluated SQL Server BI tools


We checked each vendor’s official documentation and pricing pages on November 17, 2026, against five criteria:


1. **Deployment coverage:** on-premises SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, and Azure SQL Managed Instance, plus what the tool needs to reach a server behind a firewall.
2. **Query model:** live queries against SQL Server, in-memory imports, or scheduled extracts, and how often data refreshes.
3. **Authentication:** SQL Server logins, Windows authentication, and Microsoft Entra ID, which decides whether the database can see who is asking.
4. **Security:** row-level security per viewer, SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning.
5. **Price, AI, and self-hosting:** a published starting price, what the AI features actually do, and whether you can run the tool on your own servers.


## What changed for SQL Server reporting in 2026


Microsoft’s consolidation FAQ states that “starting with SQL Server 2025, Microsoft is consolidating all on-premises reporting services under Power BI Report Server (PBIRS). No new versions of SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) will be released” ([Reporting Services consolidation FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/reporting-services/reporting-services-consolidation-faq) ). Power BI Report Server is now available to SQL Server 2025 Enterprise and Standard customers.


Teams that used SSRS mainly for dashboards now have a natural moment to compare modern BI tools. If your main need is pixel-perfect paginated reports, see our[guide to SQL reporting tools that replace SSRS and Crystal Reports](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-sql-reporting-tools-to-replace-ssrs-and-crystal-reports-2026) instead.

## Power BI: best for Microsoft 365 organizations


**Best for:** companies already on Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, especially those on Azure SQL. **Not ideal for:** small teams that want to share dashboards without paying for every viewer, or teams that don’t want to run a gateway.


- **Pricing:** Pro is $14 and Premium Per User is $24 per user per month, paid yearly. The free account can’t share reports, and viewing without a paid license needs Fabric F64 or Premium P1 capacity ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[SQL Server connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/sql-server) supports Import and DirectQuery with database, Windows, organizational account, and service principal sign-in. On-premises servers need an[on-premises data gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data) before you can schedule refresh.
- **Refresh:** shared capacity allows eight scheduled refreshes a day; Premium, PPU, and Fabric capacity allow 48. DirectQuery skips the limit by querying SQL Server on each interaction.
- **Security:**[DAX row-level security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) applies only to users with Viewer permissions, not workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors. For Azure SQL DirectQuery models,[Entra ID SSO](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-azure-sql-database-with-direct-connect) sends each viewer’s credentials, so SQL Server’s own row-level security policies apply.
- **AI:** Copilot needs[paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher, or Premium P1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) ; trial capacities and free SKUs aren’t supported.
- **Near real-time option:**[Fabric mirroring](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/mirroring/sql-server) replicates SQL Server 2016 and later into OneLake as Delta tables. Microsoft says the replication compute “is free and doesn’t consume capacity,” and each capacity unit includes 1 TB of mirroring storage.
- **Tradeoff:** embedding for customers needs an A, EM, P, or F capacity SKU, and DAX is a second language to learn on top of T-SQL.


## Tableau: best for visual analysis teams with an existing license


**Best for:** analyst teams that build exploratory visualizations and already standardize on Tableau. **Not ideal for:** teams that want AI features without upgrading to Tableau+.


- **Pricing:** Standard starts at $15 and Enterprise at $35 per user per month, billed annually ([Tableau pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) ). Creator, Explorer, and Viewer licenses are sold as separate roles, and every deployment needs at least one Creator. Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[SQL Server connector](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_sqlserver.htm) uses Windows authentication or a username and password and “does not support Microsoft Entra ID.” For Entra sign-in, use the[Azure SQL Database connector](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_azure_sql_database.htm) , which supports Active Directory password and OAuth.
- **On-premises access:** Tableau Cloud reaches private-network SQL Server through[Tableau Bridge](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/qs_refresh_local_data.htm) , which handles both live and extract connections. Tableau Server runs on your own infrastructure instead.
- **Security:**[user filters](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/publish_userfilters.htm) restrict rows per user. Connection-level data policies support SQL Server but are licensed through the Data Management add-on.
- **AI:** Tableau Pulse is included in Standard.[Tableau Agent](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein.htm) requires Tableau+ on Tableau Cloud, or Tableau Server 2025.3 and later.
- **Tradeoff:** Bridge is one more Windows service to keep running.


## Metabase: best for non-technical users on a budget


**Best for:** startups and mid-size teams that want a click-through query builder on SQL Server and an open-source option. **Not ideal for:** teams that rely on Windows authentication, or need cached models on SQL Server.


- **Pricing:** open source is free to self-host. Starter is $100 per month for 5 users plus $6 per extra user; Pro is $575 per month for 10 users plus $12 per extra user ($517.50 per month billed yearly); Enterprise starts at $20,000 per year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing) ). 14-day trial on Cloud plans. Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[SQL Server driver](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/databases/connections/sql-server) covers SQL Server and Azure SQL, with SQL Server login, Entra ID service principal, or managed identity sign-in, plus SSH tunnels. Windows authentication isn’t documented.
- **Security:**[row and column security](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/permissions/row-and-column-security) is Pro and Enterprise only and applies to the query builder.[Connection impersonation](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/permissions/impersonation) supports SQL Server, switching to a database user so SQL Server’s own permissions apply. SAML, JWT, and SCIM are Pro and Enterprise only.
- **AI:**[Metabot](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/metabot) is on every plan and creates charts from natural language, generates SQL, and fixes query errors.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on every plan (with a Metabase badge on open source and Starter), and the modular embedding SDK for React on Pro and Enterprise.
- **Tradeoff:**[model persistence](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/data-modeling/model-persistence) only works on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redshift, so heavy SQL Server models re-run their queries on each load.


For a closer look at how an AI-first tool compares, see[Basedash vs Metabase](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-metabase) .


## Grafana: best for operational dashboards and alerts


**Best for:** engineering and operations teams that want time-series dashboards and alerting on SQL Server data, including on-premises servers with Windows authentication. **Not ideal for:** business users who need per-viewer row filtering or ad hoc exploration.


- **Pricing:** self-managed Grafana OSS is free. Grafana Cloud has a free tier for 3 active users; Pro starts at $19 per month plus $8 per active user; Enterprise starts at a $25,000 yearly commit ([Grafana pricing](https://grafana.com/pricing/) ). Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[Microsoft SQL Server data source](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/mssql/) is preinstalled in Grafana OSS and Enterprise and supports SQL Server 2012 or newer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure SQL Managed Instance. It offers SQL Server authentication, Windows integrated security, Kerberos, and Entra ID, though Windows, Kerberos, and managed identity aren’t available on Grafana Cloud.
- **Querying and alerts:** a builder mode and a code mode, time macros such as` $__timeFilter` , and alerting on query results.
- **Security:** SAML, role-based access control, data source permissions, and SCIM are Enterprise and Cloud features. There’s no per-viewer row filter for SQL data sources.
- **AI:**[Grafana Assistant](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/assistant/introduction/) writes and explains SQL and can scaffold dashboards. It runs in Grafana Cloud (free for 3 AI users, then from $20 per active AI user on Pro).
- **Tradeoff:** externally[shared dashboards](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/visualizations/dashboards/share-dashboards-panels/shared-dashboards/) are read-only and don’t support variables, so customer-facing dashboards need another tool.


## Qlik Cloud Analytics: best for associative analysis across many sources


**Best for:** enterprises that combine SQL Server with ERP and CRM data and want in-memory associative exploration. **Not ideal for:** live dashboards on on-premises SQL Server behind a firewall.


- **Pricing:** Starter is $300 per month for 10 users and 10 GB of data; Standard is $825 per month for 25 GB; Premium is $2,750 per month for 50 GB, all billed annually; Enterprise is quoted ([Qlik pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ). 30-day trial. Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** Microsoft SQL Server and Azure SQL are both[Direct Query sources](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/DirectQuery/direct-access-with-direct-query.htm) . Servers behind a firewall should use the Direct Access gateway, but “it is not possible to use Qlik Data Gateway - Direct Access data connections in Direct Query,” so on-premises data has to be loaded into the app.
- **Security:**[section access](https://help.qlik.com/en-us/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Scripting/Security/manage-security-with-section-access.htm) reduces rows, columns, or both per user. SAML or OIDC SSO, and SCIM 2.0 with Entra ID.
- **AI:**[Qlik Answers](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/QlikAnswers/Qlik-Answers.htm) answers questions across structured and unstructured data.
- **Tradeoff:** pricing scales with data loaded, so large SQL Server tables raise the bill even with few users.


## Omni: best for governed self-service on Azure SQL


**Best for:** data teams on Azure SQL Database that want a shared semantic model business users can explore and ask questions of. **Not ideal for:** Azure SQL Managed Instance over Private Link, or buyers who need a published price.


- **Pricing:** not published; Omni offers a free trial through a request form ([Omni demo](https://omni.co/demo) ). Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[Microsoft SQL Server setup guide](https://docs.omni.co/connect-data/setup/microsoftsql) walks through an Azure SQL Database connection with IP allowlisting. Omni can also connect over[Azure Private Link](https://docs.omni.co/connect-data/azure-sql-privatelink) , where its docs state that “Azure SQL Managed Instance isn’t currently supported.”
- **AI:**[Omni Agent](https://docs.omni.co/ai/index) is a chat experience that generates queries, visualizations, and dashboards from questions.
- **Security:**[access_filters](https://docs.omni.co/modeling/topics/parameters/access-filters) limit rows by user attribute; SAML and SCIM guides cover Okta and Entra ID.
- **Embedding:** signed iframe URLs and the` @omni-co/embed` SDK.
- **Tradeoff:** the model-first approach pays off with a data team to maintain it, and self-hosting isn’t documented.


## Zoho Analytics: best low-cost option for small teams


**Best for:** small businesses that want SQL Server dashboards next to Zoho CRM or other SaaS data at a low published price. **Not ideal for:** teams that need live queries on Azure SQL, or SCIM provisioning.


- **Pricing:** Basic $24 (2 users), Standard $48 (5 users), Premium $115 (15 users), and Enterprise $455 (50 users) per month, billed annually; a free plan covers 2 users and 10,000 rows ([Zoho Analytics pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) ). 15-day trial. An[on-premise edition](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/onpremise-pricing.html) runs on a local server, AWS, Azure, or Docker. Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[SQL Server connector](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/import-data/local-sql-server.html) imports data on a schedule or uses Live Connect, which is “available only in paid plans and trials.” On-premises servers connect through Zoho Databridge, a utility you install on your network.[Azure SQL Database](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/cloud-database/microsoft-azure-sql-database.html) is documented as scheduled import only.
- **AI:**[Ask Zia](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/zia/) includes analysis, dashboard, and SQL agents.
- **Security:** row filters apply when sharing a view; SAML 2.0 SSO through Zoho Directory; an Embed API for embedding.
- **Tradeoff:** row filters are set per shared view rather than in a central model.


## Apache Superset: best free option for SQL-fluent teams


**Best for:** engineering-led teams that write SQL and want a free, self-hosted dashboard layer on SQL Server. **Not ideal for:** non-technical users, or teams that need SAML on a released version.


- **Pricing:** Superset is free and open source. Preset, the managed version, has a free Starter plan for up to 5 users, Professional at $20 per user per month billed annually ($25 monthly), and custom Enterprise pricing ([Preset pricing](https://preset.io/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** Superset connects through[pymssql or pyodbc](https://superset.apache.org/user-docs/databases/supported/microsoft-sql-server) . Preset lists SQL Server but[“only connects to databases that are publicly addressable”](https://docs.preset.io/docs/connecting-your-data) unless you’re on Enterprise with an SSH tunnel.
- **Security:**[row-level security filters](https://superset.apache.org/admin-docs/security/) are built into open source and assigned per dataset. Superset 6.1.0 (May 2026) is the latest release; SAML code appears in the 7.0 release candidate but isn’t in a released version yet. Preset SAML and SCIM are Enterprise only.
- **AI:** Preset’s[AI Assist](https://docs.preset.io/docs/ai-assisted-sql-querying) works with BigQuery, PostgreSQL, and Snowflake only, so it doesn’t help on SQL Server.
- **Tradeoff:** you run the web server, metadata database, and workers yourself, and scheduled reports need extra configuration.


## Basedash: best for plain-English questions on SQL Server


**Best for:** startups and mid-size companies that want an AI data analyst on SQL Server or Azure SQL without building a semantic model or DAX layer first. **Not ideal for:** per-viewer row-level security inside SQL Server, Windows authentication, or teams that want a free tier.


- **Pricing:** Startup is $1,000 per month plus AI usage for up to 25 users, including $1,000 per month in AI credits; Enterprise is custom ([Basedash pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card. Verified November 2026.
- **SQL Server support:** the[SQL Server connector](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/databases/sql-server) “connects directly and queries your data in place” and covers Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Amazon RDS for SQL Server, and Cloud SQL for SQL Server. It uses a SQL Server login (SQL Server authentication must be enabled, not only Windows authentication), with SSL and SSH tunnels for private networks.
- **AI:** the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) answers questions in chat, shows the generated SQL, and builds charts and[dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) . An[MCP server](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/mcp-server) on every plan lets Claude or ChatGPT query the same connection, and[automations](https://www.basedash.com/features/automations) can check a SQL query every 15 minutes and alert when data changes.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) is Postgres and Supabase only, so it doesn’t apply to SQL Server.[Data source access control](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/data-source-access-control) limits who can query each source and hides schemas, tables, and columns per group, including from the AI. SAML or OIDC SSO, SCIM, and audit logs are Enterprise features.
- **Deployment and embedding:**[self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/features/self-hosting) and[embedding](https://www.basedash.com/features/embedding) are Enterprise only.
- **Tradeoff:** every viewer queries through one database login, so SQL Server’s native security policies can’t tell users apart. Teams that depend on those policies are better served by Power BI with Entra SSO or Metabase impersonation.


## Which SQL Server BI tool should you choose?


**You’re on Microsoft 365 and Azure SQL.** Power BI is the default. DirectQuery with Entra ID SSO lets Azure SQL enforce its own row-level security, and Fabric mirroring gives you near real-time copies without extra compute charges.


**Your SQL Server is on-premises and you don’t want a gateway project.** Grafana, Metabase, Superset, and Basedash connect directly or over an SSH tunnel. Power BI needs the on-premises data gateway, Tableau Cloud needs Bridge, Zoho needs Databridge, and Qlik can only load on-premises data, not query it live.


**Your business users don’t write T-SQL.** Metabase’s query builder is the most approachable free option, and Metabot generates SQL on every plan. Basedash suits teams that would rather ask in plain English and read the generated SQL. Omni works well when a data team maintains a model for business users.


**Each viewer must see only their own rows.** Power BI (DAX roles, or database RLS through Entra SSO on Azure SQL), Tableau (user filters), Metabase Pro (row and column security or impersonation), Qlik (section access), and Omni (access_filters) handle this. Grafana and Basedash don’t filter rows per viewer on SQL Server. Our[row-level security comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-row-level-security-compared-2026) goes deeper on setup.


**You need alerts on operational metrics.** Grafana is built for this. Basedash automations cover business-metric alerts to email or Slack.


**You want the lowest cost.** Self-hosted Metabase, Superset, or Grafana OSS cost nothing in licenses, and Zoho Analytics has the cheapest published paid plan.


If you’re still deciding how to structure the database side, our[walkthrough on building dashboards on SQL Server data](https://www.basedash.com/blog/how-to-build-dashboards-on-sql-server-data) covers where dashboard queries should point, read-only logins, and how SQL Server’s row-level security works.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best dashboard tool for SQL Server?


It depends on your stack and users. Power BI is the most common choice for Microsoft 365 organizations: Pro costs $14 per user per month (as of November 2026), it supports Import and DirectQuery, and it can pass Entra ID identities to Azure SQL. Metabase is the most approachable option for non-technical users and is free to self-host. Grafana is best for operational dashboards with alerting. Tableau suits analyst teams focused on visual exploration, and Basedash suits teams that want to ask questions in plain English and get charts back.


### Is Microsoft discontinuing SSRS?


Microsoft isn’t removing existing SSRS installations, but it has stopped developing new versions. Its Reporting Services consolidation FAQ says that starting with SQL Server 2025, all on-premises reporting moves to Power BI Report Server, and no new versions of SSRS will be released. Power BI Report Server is available to SQL Server 2025 Enterprise and Standard customers and runs paginated RDL reports alongside Power BI reports. SSRS 2022 remains supported under its own lifecycle, so teams have time to plan a move to Power BI Report Server, the Power BI service, or another BI tool.


### Can I use Metabase with SQL Server?


Yes. Metabase has a native SQL Server driver that also works with Azure SQL Database. It supports SQL Server logins, Microsoft Entra ID service principals, and managed identity when Metabase runs in Azure, plus SSH tunnels to reach private servers. Windows authentication isn’t documented. Queries run live against the database. On Pro ($575 per month for 10 users as of November 2026) and Enterprise, Metabase adds row and column security and connection impersonation, which supports SQL Server and lets the database’s own permissions decide what each user sees.


### Which BI tools can query on-premises SQL Server without a gateway?


Tools you can run inside your own network, or that connect over an SSH tunnel, avoid a vendor gateway. Self-hosted Grafana, Metabase, and Apache Superset connect directly. Grafana also supports Windows authentication and Kerberos on self-managed installs. Basedash connects directly or through an SSH tunnel with an IP allowlist. Cloud services from Microsoft, Tableau, Qlik, and Zoho each use an agent installed on your network: the on-premises data gateway, Tableau Bridge, the Qlik Direct Access gateway, and Zoho Databridge.


### Which BI tools can use SQL Server’s own row-level security policies?


SQL Server’s native row-level security filters rows based on the database user or session context, so the BI tool must connect as each viewer rather than as one shared login. Power BI does this for Azure SQL DirectQuery models through Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on. Metabase Pro and Enterprise do it through connection impersonation, which switches to a mapped database user. Tools that use a single service login, including Grafana and Basedash, can’t pass viewer identity this way, so security has to live in the BI tool’s own permissions instead.


### What’s the difference between a SQL Server monitoring dashboard and a BI dashboard?


A monitoring dashboard tracks the health of the database server itself: CPU, memory, waits, blocking, and slow queries. SQL Server Management Studio includes a performance dashboard, and Grafana is a common choice for continuous monitoring with alerts. A BI dashboard tracks business metrics stored in the database, such as revenue, orders, or support tickets, and is built for people outside the database team. Grafana is the one tool in this comparison that does both well; the others focus on business reporting.


### Which SQL Server BI tools have AI that writes queries from plain English?


Several do, with different plan requirements as of November 2026. Metabase’s Metabot generates SQL and charts from natural language on every plan, including open source. Basedash’s AI data analyst writes SQL against SQL Server, shows the query, and returns charts on every plan. Grafana Assistant writes and explains SQL in Grafana Cloud. Power BI Copilot works on the semantic model and needs Fabric F2 or Premium P1 capacity, and Tableau Agent needs Tableau+. Preset’s AI Assist doesn’t support SQL Server; it covers BigQuery, PostgreSQL, and Snowflake.
